title.raw: 卷三百二十三 列傳第八十二 蔚昭敏 高化 周美 閻守恭 孟元 劉謙 趙振 張忠 范恪 馬懷德 安俊 向寶 Volume 323 Biographies 82: Yu Zhaomin, Gao Hua, Zhou Mei, Yan Shougong, Meng Yuan, Liu Qian, Zhao Zhen, Zhang Zhong, Fan Ke, Ma Huaide, An Jun, Xiang Bao

sentences.zh: 蔚昭敏

translations.literal: Yu Zhaomin
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhaomin

sentences.zh: 蔚昭敏，字仲明，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Yu Zhaomin, style name Zhongming, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhaomin, whose style name was Zhongming, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父興，事周世宗，數戰伐有功，又從太宗平太原，終龍尉都虞候。

translations.literal: His father Xing served Emperor Shizong of Zhou, achieved merit in many campaigns, also followed Emperor Taizong in pacifying Taiyuan, and finally ended as chief military adjutant of the Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing had served Emperor Shizong of Zhou and won distinction in repeated campaigns; he also followed Emperor Taizong in the conquest of Taiyuan and eventually rose to chief military adjutant of the Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 真宗為襄王，昭敏自東班殿侍選隸襄王府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong was Prince of Xiang, Zhaomin was selected from the Eastern Class palace attendants to serve in the Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhenzong was still Prince of Xiang, Zhaomin was chosen from the Eastern Class palace attendants and assigned to the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，授西頭供奉官，累遷崇儀使、冀貝行營兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, he was appointed Western Head Palace Attendant, and through successive promotions became Commissioner of Ceremonial Regalia and overall military supervisor of the Ji-Bei campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession he was made a Western Head Palace Attendant and was promoted in due course to Commissioner of Ceremonial Regalia and overall military supervisor of the Ji-Bei campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 契丹以五千騎突至冀州城南，昭敏帥部兵與戰，敗之，得其器甲，賊遁去，而師不失一人。

translations.literal: The Khitan with five thousand horsemen suddenly arrived south of Jizhou city; Zhaomin led his troops to engage them, defeated them, seized their weapons and armor, the bandits fled, and his army did not lose a single man.
translations.idiomatic: When five thousand Khitan horsemen suddenly appeared south of Jizhou, Zhaomin led his troops into battle, routed them, and captured their arms and armor. The enemy fled, and not one of his men was lost.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，領順州刺史、定州行營鈐轄兼押大陣，又為鎮、定、高陽關三路先鋒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he held the posts of prefect of Shunzhou, campaign headquarters military commissioner of Dingzhou and commander of the main battle array, and was also vanguard for the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Xianping era he served as prefect of Shunzhou, as campaign military commissioner at Dingzhou with command of the main army, and as vanguard for the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，帝北巡至大名，契丹退趨莫州，昭敏與范廷召追至莫州東三十里，斬首萬餘級，擒生口甚眾，契丹委器甲遁去。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, the Emperor made a northern tour as far as Daming; the Khitan withdrew toward Mozhou; Zhaomin and Fan Tingzhao pursued them to thirty li east of Mozhou, beheaded more than ten thousand, captured very many prisoners alive, and the Khitan abandoned weapons and armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: During a Khitan invasion the emperor advanced north as far as Daming. As the Khitan withdrew toward Mozhou, Zhaomin and Fan Tingzhao pursued them thirty li east of Mozhou, took more than ten thousand heads, and captured a great number of prisoners. The Khitan abandoned their arms and armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 拜唐州團練使，累遷至殿前副都指揮使，遷都指揮使、保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed regimental commissioner of Tangzhou, and through successive promotions reached vice overall commander of the Palace Front, then overall commander and military governor of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regimental commissioner of Tangzhou, rose through successive promotions to vice overall commander of the Palace Front Division, and was then made overall commander and military governor of the Baojing army.

sentences.zh: 以足疾，命入謁無拜。

translations.literal: Because of illness in his feet, he was ordered that on entering audience he need not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a foot ailment, he was excused from bowing when he came to court.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He died, and was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高化，字仲熙，真定人。

translations.literal: Gao Hua, style name Zhongxi, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hua, whose style name was Zhongxi, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 少沉勇有力，不事耕稼，學擊劍，善射。

translations.literal: In youth he was steady, brave, and strong; he did not engage in farming, studied swordplay, and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was steady, brave, and powerful. He did not work the fields but trained in swordsmanship and became an expert archer.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯河北，應募轉餉飛狐口。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded Hebei, he answered the call to transport provisions to Feihukou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded Hebei, he volunteered to transport supplies to Feihukou.

sentences.zh: 楊業留戲下，使捕賊酋大鵬翼，獲之。

translations.literal: Yang Ye kept him in his retinue and had him capture the bandit chieftain Dapengyi; he obtained him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye kept him in his service and sent him to capture the rebel chieftain Dapengyi, whom he took alive.

sentences.zh: 會契丹又犯真定，乃辭業還家，家屬盡為契丹所掠去。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan again invaded Zhending; he then took leave of Ye and returned home, and his entire family was carried off by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded Zhending again, he left Yang Ye's service and went home, only to find that the Khitan had carried off his entire family.

sentences.zh: 從州將入京師，遂隸禁軍，選為襄王牽䪊官。

translations.literal: He followed the prefectural commander into the capital, then entered the Palace Army, and was selected as horse-handler for the Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed a prefectural commander to the capital, entered the Palace Army, and was chosen as groom for the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 王尹京，命巡內外八廂，積獲奸盜甚眾。

translations.literal: When the prince governed the capital, he was ordered to patrol the inner and outer eight wards and over time captured very many thieves and villains.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince served as mayor of the capital, he was ordered to patrol the eight inner and outer wards of the city and over time captured a great many criminals.

sentences.zh: 盜有遺化金帛者，化弗受。

translations.literal: When thieves offered Hua gold and silks, Hua would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves sometimes offered him gold and silks, but he refused to take them.

sentences.zh: 一日，王趨急召出府門，馬驚墮，化掖之而起。

translations.literal: One day the prince hurried out at an urgent summons beyond the mansion gate; his horse startled and he fell; Hua supported him and helped him rise.
translations.idiomatic: One day the prince rushed out at an urgent summons beyond the mansion gate. His horse bolted and threw him, but Hua caught him and helped him to his feet.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「微爾。

translations.literal: The prince said: "But for you.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "But for you,

sentences.zh: 吾幾殆。

translations.literal: I would nearly have perished.
translations.idiomatic: I would have been killed.

sentences.zh: 」益親信之。

translations.literal: " He trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " After that he trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 發兵襲明珠族，不利，降滑州總管。

translations.literal: He sent troops to attack the Mingzhu tribe; the outcome was unfavorable, and he was demoted to commandant of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops against the Mingzhu tribe, but the campaign went badly and he was transferred to serve as commandant of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 改興州防禦使、真定路副都總管，徙高陽關路。

translations.literal: He was changed to defense commissioner of Xingzhou and vice overall commander of the Zhending route, then transferred to the Gaoyang Pass route.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defense commissioner of Xingzhou and vice overall commander of the Zhending circuit, then transferred to the Gaoyang Pass circuit.

sentences.zh: 修護章惠太后園陵，累拜殿前副都指揮使，歷建武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He repaired and guarded the garden tomb of Empress Dowager Zhanghui, and through successive appointments became vice overall commander of the Palace Front and served as military governor of Jianwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw repairs at the garden tomb of Empress Dowager Zhanghui, rose through successive promotions to vice overall commander of the Palace Front Division, and served as military governor of the Jianwu army.

sentences.zh: 以老，辭管軍。

translations.literal: Because of age, he resigned from managing the army.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew old he asked to be relieved of command of the army.

sentences.zh: 詔入朝，化又固請，改武安軍節度使、知滄州，未行，改相州。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him to court; Hua again firmly requested leave, was changed to military governor of Wu'an Army and prefect of Cangzhou, had not yet departed when he was changed to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court, but Hua again pressed his request to retire. He was appointed military governor of the Wu'an army and prefect of Cangzhou, but before he could take up the post he was reassigned to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 部有大獄已具，皆當論死。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction there was a major case already concluded, and all were to be sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In his jurisdiction a major trial had already been concluded, and every defendant was to be sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 化疑之，遣移訊，果出無罪者三人。

translations.literal: Hua doubted it, sent it for reinvestigation, and indeed three innocent persons were found.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had doubts about the case and ordered a reinvestigation, which revealed three men who were in fact innocent.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復告老，以右屯衛上將軍致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again reported old age and retired with the title of senior general of the Right Unicorn Guard.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he again asked to retire and was granted retirement with the rank of senior general of the Right Unicorn Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰恭莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Commandant, with posthumous title Respectful and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant with the posthumous title Respectful and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 化謹質少過，馭軍有法。

translations.literal: Hua was careful and plain, with few faults, and governed the army by rule.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was careful and upright, seldom at fault, and disciplined his troops by strict rules.

sentences.zh: 雖起身行伍，然頗知民事焉。

translations.literal: Although he rose from the ranks, he nevertheless understood civilian affairs rather well.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had risen from the ranks, he understood civilian affairs remarkably well.

sentences.zh: 周美，字之純，靈州回樂人。

translations.literal: Zhou Mei, style name Zhichun, was a native of Huile in Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mei, whose style name was Zhichun, came from Huile in Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少隸朔方軍，以材武稱。

translations.literal: In youth he served in the Shuofang Army and was famed for talent and martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served in the Shuofang army and won renown for his ability and fighting skill.

sentences.zh: 趙保吉陷靈州，美棄其族，間走歸京師，天子召見，隸禁軍。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baoji seized Lingzhou, Mei abandoned his clan, made his way by secret paths back to the capital, the Son of Heaven summoned him for audience, and he entered the Palace Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baoji seized Lingzhou, Mei left his clan behind, made his way secretly back to the capital, was received in audience by the emperor, and entered the Palace Army.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯邊，真宗幸澶州，禦城北門，美慷慨自陳，願假數騎縛契丹將至闕下，帝壯之，常令宿衛。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the border, Emperor Zhenzong visited Chanyuan and defended the north gate of the city; Mei spoke forth boldly on his own behalf, wishing to borrow a few horsemen to bind a Khitan general and bring him beneath the palace gates; the Emperor was impressed by his spirit and often had him remain on night guard.
translations.idiomatic: During a Khitan border raid, Emperor Zhenzong went to Chanyuan and took his stand at the city's north gate. Mei stepped forward boldly and declared that, given a few horsemen, he would bind a Khitan general and bring him to the palace gates. The emperor was stirred by his daring and often kept him on night guard.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，德明部落寇平涼方渠，美以軍候戍邊，與州將追戰，破之於九井原、烏侖河，斬首甚眾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, the tribes of Deming raided Pingliang and Fangqu; Mei served as army scout on the border garrison, pursued battle with the prefectural commander, and defeated them at Jiujing Plain and Wulun River, beheading very many.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiansheng era, Deming's tribes raided Pingliang and Fangqu. Mei served as an army scout on the frontier and, together with the prefectural commander, pursued the enemy and defeated them at Jiujing Plain and on the Wulun River, taking a great many heads.

sentences.zh: 累遷天武都虞候。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became chief military adjutant of the Heavenly Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to chief military adjutant of the Heavenly Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，陝西用兵，經略使夏竦薦其材，擢供備庫使、延州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao rebelled and troops were used in Shaanxi, frontier commissioner Xia Song recommended his talent; he was promoted to commissioner of the supply depot and overall military supervisor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled and war broke out in Shaanxi, frontier commissioner Xia Song recommended him for his ability. He was promoted to commissioner of the supply depot and overall military supervisor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人既破金明諸砦，美請於經略使范仲淹曰：「夏人新得志，其勢必復來。

translations.literal: After the Xia people had broken the Jinming stockades and others, Mei requested of frontier commissioner Fan Zhongyan: "The Xia people have newly gained their ambition; their momentum will surely bring them back.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xia had overrun the Jinming stockades and others, Mei urged frontier commissioner Fan Zhongyan, "The Xia are riding high on victory and will surely return.

sentences.zh: 金明當邊衝，我之蔽也，今不亟完，將遂失之。

translations.literal: Jinming stands on the frontier pass; it is our screen. If we do not quickly complete it now, we will soon lose it.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming lies on a critical frontier pass and is our shield. If we do not repair it at once, we shall lose it for good."

sentences.zh: 」仲淹因屬美復城如故。

translations.literal: " Zhongyan therefore entrusted Mei to restore the city as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan therefore put Mei in charge of rebuilding the city as it had been.

sentences.zh: 數日賊果來，其眾數萬薄金明，陣於延安城北三十里。

translations.literal: Within several days the bandits indeed came; their force of tens of thousands pressed Jinming and formed battle lines thirty li north of Yan'an city.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the enemy did come. Tens of thousands of them pressed Jinming and drew up in battle order thirty li north of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 美領眾二千力戰，抵暮，援兵不至，乃徙軍山北，多設疑兵。

translations.literal: Mei led two thousand men in fierce fighting until evening; relief troops did not arrive; he then moved his army north of the mountain and set up many decoy forces.
translations.idiomatic: Mei led two thousand men in a hard fight until evening, but no reinforcements came. He then shifted his army to the north side of the mountain and set up many decoy detachments.

sentences.zh: 夏人望見，以為救至，即引去。

translations.literal: The Xia people saw them and thought relief had arrived, and immediately withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia saw them, took them for arriving reinforcements, and withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 既而復出艾蒿砦，遂至郭北平，夜鬥不解。

translations.literal: Before long they again came out from Aigao Stockade, then reached Guobei Plain, and night fighting did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they emerged again from Aigao Stockade and advanced to Guobei Plain, where fighting raged through the night without pause.

sentences.zh: 美率眾使人持一炬從間道上山，益張旗幟，四面大噪，賊懼走。

translations.literal: Mei led his troops and had men carry a single torch up the mountain by a hidden path, further spread banners and flags, raised a great clamor on all four sides, and the bandits fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Mei led his men up a hidden path, each carrying a torch, spread more banners, and raised a deafening shout on every side. The enemy fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 獲牛羊、橐駝、鎧甲數千計，遂募兵築萬安城而還。

translations.literal: They obtained cattle, sheep, camels, and armor numbering in the thousands; he then recruited troops, built Wan'an city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They captured thousands of cattle, sheep, camels, and suits of armor. Mei then recruited troops, built Wan'an city, and returned.

sentences.zh: 敵復寇金明，美引兵由虞家堡並北山而下，敵即引卻。

translations.literal: The enemy again raided Jinming; Mei led troops down from Yujia Fort along the northern mountain, and the enemy immediately withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy raided Jinming again, Mei led his troops down from Yujia Fort along the northern hills, and the enemy withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 遷文思使，徙知保定軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Literary Accomplishment Commissioner and moved to govern Baoding Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Literary Accomplishment Commissioner and appointed to govern Baoding Army.

sentences.zh: 經略使龐籍表留之，改東路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Frontier commissioner Pang Ji memorialized to retain him; he was changed to overall eastern-route inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commissioner Pang Ji petitioned to keep him in the region, and he was made overall inspector of the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 敗敵於金湯城，焚其族部二十一。

translations.literal: He defeated the enemy at Jintang city and burned twenty-one of their tribal encampments.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the enemy at Jintang city and burned twenty-one of their tribal settlements.

sentences.zh: 元昊大入，據承平砦。

translations.literal: Yuanhao made a major invasion and occupied Chenping Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao launched a major invasion and seized Chenping Stockade.

sentences.zh: 諸將會兵議攻討，洛苑副使种世衡請齎三日糧直搗敵穴。

translations.literal: The generals gathered troops to discuss attack; Luoyuan vice commissioner Zhong Shihang requested to carry three days' provisions and strike straight at the enemy's lair.
translations.idiomatic: The generals assembled their forces to plan an attack. Luoyuan vice commissioner Zhong Shihang proposed taking three days' rations and striking straight at the enemy stronghold.

sentences.zh: 美曰：「彼知吾來，必設伏待我。

translations.literal: Mei said: "They will know we are coming and will surely set ambushes to wait for us.
translations.idiomatic: Mei said, "They will know we are coming and are sure to lay ambushes for us.

sentences.zh: 不如間道掩其不意。

translations.literal: It would be better to take a hidden path and strike where they do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take a hidden route and fall on them unawares."

sentences.zh: 」世衡不聽。

translations.literal: " Shihang did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shihang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 美獨以兵西出芙蓉谷，大破敵。

translations.literal: Mei alone led troops west out through Furong Valley and inflicted a great defeat on the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Mei alone led his troops west through Furong Valley and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 世衡等果無功。

translations.literal: Shihang and the others indeed achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: Shihang and the others, as it turned out, accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敵復略土塠砦，美迎擊於野家店，追北至拓跋谷，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy again raided Tudun Stockade; Mei met them in attack at Yejia Inn, pursued north to the Tuoba Valley, and inflicted a great defeat on their force.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy raided Tudun Stockade again. Mei met them at Yejia Inn, pursued them north to Tuoba Valley, and crushed their force.

sentences.zh: 以功遷右騏驥使。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Right Qiji Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was promoted to Right Qiji Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 軍還，築柵於蔥梅官道谷，以據敵路。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he built a palisade in Congmei Official Road Valley to hold the enemy's route.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he built a stockade in Congmei Official Road Valley to block the enemy's line of advance.

sentences.zh: 令士卒益種營田，而收穀六千斛。

translations.literal: He ordered the soldiers to increase planting of garrison fields, and harvested six thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He had his soldiers expand the garrison farms and harvested six thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 復率眾繇廳子部西濟大理河，屠劄萬多移二百帳，焚其積聚以歸。

translations.literal: Again he led his force west from Tingzi tribe, crossed the Dali River, slaughtered more than two hundred tents of the Zha Wanduoyi tribe, burned their stores, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He again led his troops west from the Tingzi tribe, crossed the Dali River, destroyed more than two hundred tents of the Zha Wanduoyi tribe, burned their stores, and returned.

sentences.zh: 籍、仲淹交薦之，除鄜延路兵馬都監，遷賀州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji and Zhongyan both recommended him in turn; he was appointed overall military supervisor of the Fuyan route and transferred to prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Zhongyan both recommended him, and he was made overall military supervisor of the Fuyan circuit and then prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，美自靈武來，上其所服精甲，詔藏軍器庫。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mei came from Lingwu, he presented the fine armor he wore; an edict ordered it stored in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: When Mei first came from Lingwu he presented the fine armor he wore, and an edict ordered it stored in the imperial armory.

sentences.zh: 至是，加飾黃金，遣使即軍中賜之。

translations.literal: At this time gold ornament was added, and envoys were sent to bestow it upon him right in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Now it was trimmed with gold and an envoy was sent to present it to him in camp.

sentences.zh: 又破敵於無定河，乘勝至綏州，殺其酋豪，焚廬帳，獲牛馬、羊駝、器械三百計，因城龍口平砦。

translations.literal: Again he defeated the enemy on the Wuding River, pressed the victory to Suizhou, killed their chieftains and notables, burned their tents and lodges, obtained cattle, horses, sheep, camels, and weapons numbering about three hundred, and thereby fortified Longkou Ping Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the enemy on the Wuding River, pressed the victory to Suizhou, killed their chieftains, burned their camps, and captured some three hundred head of cattle, horses, sheep, and camels along with weapons. He then fortified Longkou Ping Stockade.

sentences.zh: 敵以精騎數千來襲，美從百餘騎馳擊破之。

translations.literal: The enemy with several thousand elite horsemen came to attack; Mei with a little more than a hundred horsemen charged and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand elite enemy horsemen attacked, Mei with a little over a hundred horsemen charged and routed them.

sentences.zh: 加本路鈐轄，遂為副總管。

translations.literal: He was added as military commissioner of this route, and then became vice overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the circuit and then vice overall commander.

sentences.zh: 遷龍神衛四廂都指揮使、通州刺史；

translations.literal: He was transferred to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and prefect of Tongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and made prefect of Tongzhou;

sentences.zh: 進捧日、天武四廂都指揮使，陵州團練使。

translations.literal: he advanced to overall commander of the four wings of the Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial guards and regimental commissioner of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: then advanced to overall commander of the four wings of the Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial guards and regimental commissioner of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，又城清水、安定、黑水、佛堂、北橫山、乾谷、土明、柳谷、雕巢、盧兒、原安砦十一堡。

translations.literal: During Qingli he again fortified eleven stockades: Qingshui, Anding, Heishui, Fotang, North Hengshan, Qian'gu, Tuming, Liugu, Diaochao, Lu'er, and Yuan'an.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era he fortified eleven more stockades: Qingshui, Anding, Heishui, Fotang, North Hengshan, Qian'gu, Tuming, Liugu, Diaochao, Lu'er, and Yuan'an.

sentences.zh: 安定之役，諜報敵數萬將大至，經略使遣管勾機宜楚建中分諸將兵，趣城黑水以待。

translations.literal: In the Anding campaign, spies reported that enemy forces numbering tens of thousands would arrive in strength; the frontier commissioner sent staff officer Chu Jianzhong to divide the generals' troops and hurry to fortify Heishui to await them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Anding campaign, intelligence reported that tens of thousands of enemy troops were about to arrive. The frontier commissioner sent staff officer Chu Jianzhong to divide the generals' forces and hurry to Heishui to hold the city against them.

sentences.zh: 諸將憚敵且至，不肯與兵。

translations.literal: The generals feared the enemy would soon arrive and were unwilling to give troops.
translations.idiomatic: The generals feared the enemy's imminent arrival and refused to detach troops.

sentences.zh: 美曰：「兵常以寡擊眾，何自怯也。

translations.literal: Mei said: "Armies constantly use the few to strike the many—why be timid on your own account?
translations.idiomatic: Mei said, "Soldiers are meant to strike many with few—why shrink back now?

sentences.zh: 」卒以兵二千與建中，而敵亦引去。

translations.literal: " In the end he gave Chu two thousand troops, and the enemy also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he gave Chu two thousand men, and the enemy withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 每邊書至，諸將各擇便利，獨美未嘗辭難，然所向輒克，諸將以此服之。

translations.literal: Whenever frontier dispatches arrived, each general chose what was convenient; only Mei never declined hardship, yet wherever he went he invariably prevailed, and the generals for this reason submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever frontier dispatches arrived, the other generals chose the easier assignments, but Mei never shirked a hard task. Wherever he went he prevailed, and for this the other generals came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 歷侍衛親軍馬軍殿前都虞候、眉州防禦使、步軍副都指揮使、遂州觀察使、鄜延副都總管。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of chief military adjutant of the Palace Cavalry in the Imperial Guard, defense commissioner of Meizhou, vice overall commander of the Foot Soldiers, observation commissioner of Suizhou, and vice overall commander of Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as chief military adjutant of the Palace Cavalry in the Imperial Guard, defense commissioner of Meizhou, vice overall commander of the Foot Soldiers, observation commissioner of Suizhou, and vice overall commander of Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 召還，授耀州觀察使，又進馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was recalled, appointed observation commissioner of Yaozhou, and again advanced to vice overall commander of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court, appointed observation commissioner of Yaozhou, and promoted again to vice overall commander of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈忠武軍節度使，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given military governor of Zhongwu Army, with posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as military governor of the Zhongwu army with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 自陝西用兵，諸將多不利，美前後十餘戰，平族帳二百，焚二十一，招種落內附者十一族，復城堡甚多。

translations.literal: Since troops were used in Shaanxi, most generals fared poorly; Mei in more than ten battles before and after pacified two hundred tribal tents, burned twenty-one, induced eleven tribes of various clans to submit inward, and restored very many castles and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Shaanxi campaigns began, most generals had fared poorly, but Mei fought more than a dozen engagements, subdued two hundred tribal encampments, burned twenty-one, brought eleven tribes in submission, and restored a great many forts and stockades.

sentences.zh: 在軍中所得祿賜，多分其戲下，有餘，悉饗勞之。

translations.literal: The salary and gifts he received in the army he mostly divided among his subordinates; what remained he entirely used to feast and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: He gave most of his salary and rewards in the army to his men, and whatever remained he spent entirely on feasting and rewarding them.

sentences.zh: 及死，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: When he died, his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his family had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 子蚤卒，以孫永清為子，官至引進副使。

translations.literal: His son died young; he took his grandson Yongqing as son, who reached the office of vice commissioner of presentation.
translations.idiomatic: His son died young, so he adopted his grandson Yongqing, who rose to vice commissioner of presentation.

sentences.zh: 閻守恭

translations.literal: Yan Shougong
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shougong

sentences.zh: 閻守恭，并州榆次人。

translations.literal: Yan Shougong was a native of Yuci in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shougong came from Yuci in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父榮，倜儻有志略，劉繼元欲召至帳下，辭以母老不就。

translations.literal: His father Rong was free-spirited and had will and strategy; Liu Jiyuan wished to summon him to his headquarters, but he declined on the grounds that his mother was old and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong was bold and enterprising. Liu Jiyuan wished to summon him to his staff, but he declined on the ground that his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 守恭生而體貌奇偉，榮曰：「是必當事太平天子，吾無恨矣。

translations.literal: Shougong from birth had an extraordinary stature; Rong said: "This one will surely serve the Son of Heaven of the Great Peace—I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Shougong was born with an imposing physique. Rong said, "This boy is bound to serve the emperor of a peaceful age. I shall have no regrets."

sentences.zh: 」後十七年，劉氏平，徙太原民於大名府，因家焉。

translations.literal: " Seventeen years later the Liu house was pacified; the people of Taiyuan were moved to Daming Prefecture, and they made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years later the Liu regime fell. The people of Taiyuan were relocated to Daming Prefecture, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 往來負販於並、汾間，過西山，聞郭進為都巡檢使，太宗甚寵遇之。

translations.literal: Going back and forth carrying goods for sale between Bing and Fen, he passed the Western Hills and heard that Guo Jin was overall inspector and that Emperor Taizong greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled as a peddler between Bing and Fen. Passing the Western Hills, he heard that Guo Jin was overall inspector and that Emperor Taizong favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 乃慨然曰：「進不遇主，亦行伍爾，吾自度豈不及進邪？

translations.literal: He then said with emotion: "If Jin had not met his lord, he too would be only in the ranks—do I not measure myself as no less than Jin?
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "If Jin had not found his sovereign, he too would be nothing but a common soldier. Why should I not measure up to Jin?"

sentences.zh: 」遂應募，隸拱聖軍，擢殿前押班。

translations.literal: " He then answered the call, entered the Palatine Sacred Army, and was promoted to palace-front escort leader.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted, joined the Palatine Sacred Army, and was promoted to palace-front escort leader.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，從幸河北，以功為捧日副指揮使，歷拱聖、龍衛、捧日指揮使，累遷左第二軍指揮使、乾州刺史。

translations.literal: During Xianping he followed the imperial tour to Hebei; for merit he became vice commander of the Sun-Bearer Guard, successively served as commander of the Palatine Sacred, Dragon Guard, and Sun-Bearer guards, and through promotions became commander of the Left Second Army and prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he accompanied the emperor to Hebei. For his achievements he was made vice commander of the Sun-Bearer Guard and served in turn as commander of the Palatine Sacred, Dragon Guard, and Sun-Bearer guards before rising to commander of the Left Second Army and prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 明道中，落軍職，以德州刺史為永興軍兵馬鈐轄，徙幷代路。

translations.literal: During Mingdao he was removed from army office and, as prefect of Dezhou, became military commissioner of Yongxing Army, then was transferred to the Bing-Dai route.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingdao era he left active army command and, as prefect of Dezhou, was appointed military commissioner of Yongxing Army, then transferred to the Bing-Dai circuit.

sentences.zh: 守恭性沉勇，御軍嚴。

translations.literal: Shougong by nature was steady and brave and governed the army strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Shougong was by nature steady and brave and ruled his troops with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 雖家居如對賓客。

translations.literal: Even at home he was as if facing guests.
translations.idiomatic: Even at home he conducted himself as if he were receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 常訪求士大夫，取郭進事而師法之。

translations.literal: He constantly sought out scholar-officials, took Guo Jin's conduct as his model, and followed his example.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly sought out scholar-officials and took Guo Jin's career as his model to emulate.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿悉散予人。

translations.literal: All the salary and stipends he received he entirely distributed to others.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away all his salary and stipends to others.

sentences.zh: 在并州，因春社會賓客曰：「守恭，太原一貧民爾。

translations.literal: While in Bingzhou, on the spring community sacrifice he gathered guests and said: "Shougong is only a poor commoner of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: While in Bingzhou, at the spring community sacrifice he entertained his guests and said, "Shougong is only a poor man from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 徒步位刺史，老復官鄉里，逾分多矣。

translations.literal: On foot I reached the rank of prefect; in old age I return to office in my home district—this is already far beyond my due.
translations.idiomatic: I rose on foot to the rank of prefect, and now in old age I am returning to serve in my home district—already far more than I deserve.

sentences.zh: 今日與卿輩訣。

translations.literal: Today I take leave of you all.
translations.idiomatic: Today I bid you farewell.

sentences.zh: 」後十日卒。

translations.literal: " Ten days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he died.

sentences.zh: 孟元，字善長，洺州人。

translations.literal: Meng Yuan, style name Shanchang, was a native of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yuan, whose style name was Shanchang, came from Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 性謹願少過，頗喜讀書。

translations.literal: By nature he was careful and sincere with few faults, and rather enjoyed reading books.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature careful and upright, seldom at fault, and fond of reading.

sentences.zh: 少隸禁軍，以挽強選補殿侍，累遷散都頭班指揮使，擢如京使、幷代州兵馬都監，改鈐轄，徙高陽關路，又徙真定路。

translations.literal: In youth he served in the Palace Army; for drawing the strong bow he was selected and appointed palace attendant, through successive promotions became commander of the Scattered Chief Squad, was promoted to Capital Envoy and overall military supervisor of Bing-Dai prefecture, changed to military commissioner, transferred to Gaoyang Pass route, then again to Zhending route.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he entered the Palace Army. Selected for his skill at drawing the heavy bow, he became a palace attendant and rose through successive promotions to commander of the Scattered Chief Squad. He was then made Capital Envoy and overall military supervisor of Bing-Dai prefecture, appointed military commissioner, transferred to the Gaoyang Pass circuit, and then to the Zhending circuit.

sentences.zh: 王則據貝州反，元赴城下攻戰，被數十創，又中機石，墜濠中。

translations.literal: Wang Ze seized Beizhou and rebelled; Yuan went beneath the city wall to attack in battle, received several tens of wounds, was also struck by a catapult stone, and fell into the moat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze seized Beizhou and rebelled, Yuan fought at the foot of the city walls. He suffered dozens of wounds, was struck by a catapult stone, and fell into the moat.

sentences.zh: 既出，戰愈力。

translations.literal: Once he got out, he fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Once he climbed out, he fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 更募死士由永濟渠穴地以進。

translations.literal: He further recruited dare-to-die troops to advance by tunneling along the Yongji Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He then recruited dare-to-die troops to tunnel along the Yongji Canal and advance into the city.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改右騏驥使，徙大名府路鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was changed to Right Qiji Commissioner and transferred to military commissioner of Daming Prefecture route.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was made Right Qiji Commissioner and transferred to military commissioner of the Daming Prefecture circuit.

sentences.zh: 河朔饑，權知滄州。

translations.literal: When Heshuo suffered famine, he was acting prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Heshuo, he served as acting prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 民鬻鹽為生，歲荒鹽多不售，民無以自給。

translations.literal: The people sold salt to make a living; in years of famine the salt often would not sell, and the people had no means to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The people made their living by selling salt, but in years of famine salt often would not sell and they could not support themselves.

sentences.zh: 元度軍食有餘，悉用易鹽，繇是民不轉徙。

translations.literal: Yuan estimated that army provisions were in surplus and entirely used them to exchange for salt; thereby the people did not migrate away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan found that army provisions were in surplus and used them all to buy the people's salt, so the people did not have to flee the region.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞郭勸言其貝州功而賞未當，乃擢普州刺史，遷宮苑使，專管勾麟府軍馬事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Guo Quan said his merit at Beizhou had not been properly rewarded; he was then promoted to prefect of Puzhou, transferred to Palace Park Commissioner, and exclusively managed Linfu army and horse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Guo Quan argued that his achievements at Beizhou had not been properly rewarded. He was promoted to prefect of Puzhou, made Palace Park Commissioner, and put in charge of Linfu army and horse affairs.

sentences.zh: 護築永寧堡，敵不敢動。

translations.literal: He oversaw construction of Yongning Fort; the enemy did not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the building of Yongning Fort, and the enemy did not dare move against it.

sentences.zh: 為龍神衛四廂都指揮使、忠州團練使、高陽關馬步軍總管，遷天武、捧日四廂都指揮使，又遷步軍都虞候、眉州防禦使、幷代路副都總管。

translations.literal: He became overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, regimental commissioner of Zhongzhou, and overall commander of cavalry and infantry at Gaoyang Pass; was transferred to overall commander of the four wings of the Heavenly Martial and Sun-Bearer guards; again transferred to chief military adjutant of the Foot Soldiers, defense commissioner of Meizhou, and vice overall commander of the Bing-Dai route.
translations.idiomatic: He became overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, regimental commissioner of Zhongzhou, and overall commander of cavalry and infantry at Gaoyang Pass. He was then made overall commander of the four wings of the Heavenly Martial and Sun-Bearer guards, and later chief military adjutant of the Foot Soldiers, defense commissioner of Meizhou, and vice overall commander of the Bing-Dai circuit.

sentences.zh: 判北京賈昌朝奏為大名府路副都總管，徙定州路，遷馬軍都虞候，徙鄜延路，行至鄭州卒，贈遂州觀察使。

translations.literal: Administrator of Northern Capital Jia Changchao memorialized him as vice overall commander of Daming Prefecture route; he was moved to Dingzhou route, promoted to chief military adjutant of the Cavalry, transferred to Fuyan route, died on the road at Zhengzhou, and was posthumously given observation commissioner of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of the Northern Capital Jia Changchao recommended him as vice overall commander of the Daming Prefecture circuit. He was transferred to the Dingzhou circuit, promoted to chief military adjutant of the Cavalry, then moved to the Fuyan circuit. He died on the road at Zhengzhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as observation commissioner of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 劉謙，字漢宗，開封人。

translations.literal: Liu Qian, style name Hanzong, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qian, whose style name was Hanzong, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少補衛士，數遷至捧日右廂都指揮使，領嘉州團練使兼京城巡檢。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the guard corps; through several promotions he reached overall commander of the Right Wing of the Sun-Bearer Guard, holding regimental commissioner of Jiazhou and concurrently capital patrol inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he joined the guard corps and rose through several promotions to overall commander of the Right Wing of the Sun-Bearer Guard, serving as regimental commissioner of Jiazhou and concurrently as capital patrol inspector.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，改博州團練使、環慶路馬步軍總管兼知邠州。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was changed to regimental commissioner of Bozhou, overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Huanqing route, and concurrently prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was made regimental commissioner of Bozhou, overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Huanqing circuit, and concurrently prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 謙不讀書，然鬥訟曲直，皆區處當理。

translations.literal: Qian did not read books, yet in disputes over right and wrong he always judged and disposed of matters according to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was not a reader, yet in civil disputes he always judged cases fairly and according to reason.

sentences.zh: 前守者多強市民物以飾廚傳，謙獨無所撓，邠人頗愛之。

translations.literal: Earlier prefects mostly forcibly bought goods from the people to furnish their kitchens and travel supplies; Qian alone did nothing of the sort, and the people of Bin greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier prefects had often forced the people to supply goods for their kitchens and travel expenses, but Qian did nothing of the kind, and the people of Bin came to esteem him.

sentences.zh: 夏竦奏為涇原路總管，徙知涇州，未行，會賊寇鎮戎軍，謙引兵深入賊境，破其聚落而還。

translations.literal: Xia Song memorialized him as overall commander of Jingyuan route; he was transferred to govern Jingzhou; had not yet departed when bandits raided Zhenrong Army; Qian led troops deep into enemy territory, broke their settlements, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song recommended him as overall commander of the Jingyuan circuit and appointed him to govern Jingzhou. Before he could depart, bandits raided Zhenrong Army. Qian led his troops deep into enemy territory, destroyed their settlements, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以功擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、象州防禦使。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 暴疾卒，贈永清軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: He died suddenly of illness and was posthumously given military governor and observation regent of Yongqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as military governor and observation regent of the Yongqing army.

sentences.zh: 趙振，字仲威，雄州歸信人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhen, style name Zhongwei, was a native of Guixin in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhen, whose style name was Zhongwei, came from Guixin in Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德中，從石普於順安軍。

translations.literal: During Jingde he followed Shi Pu at Shun'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era he served under Shi Pu at Shun'an Army.

sentences.zh: 獲契丹陣圖，授三班借職。

translations.literal: He captured a Khitan battle map and was given a borrowed post in the Third Class.
translations.idiomatic: He captured a Khitan battle map and was granted a borrowed post in the Third Class.

sentences.zh: 後數年，為隰州兵馬監押，捕盜於青灰山，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Several years later he was military supervisor of Xi prefecture; he captured bandits at Qinghui Mountain and killed or captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, as military supervisor of Xi prefecture, he hunted bandits on Qinghui Mountain and killed or captured a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 高平蠻叛，徙湖北都巡檢使兼制置南路。

translations.literal: When the Gaoping tribes rebelled, he was transferred to overall inspector of Hubei and concurrently commissioner for organizing the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaoping tribes rebelled, he was made overall inspector of Hubei and concurrently commissioner for organizing the southern route.

sentences.zh: 以南方暑濕，弓弩不利，別創小矢，激三百步，中輒洞穿，蠻遂駭散。

translations.literal: Because the south was hot and damp and crossbows were ineffective, he separately devised small arrows that could be shot three hundred paces; when they hit they pierced straight through, and the tribes were terrified and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Because the southern climate was hot and damp and crossbows performed poorly there, he devised special short arrows that could be shot three hundred paces and pierced clean through on impact. The tribes were terrified and scattered.

sentences.zh: 歲中，遷慶州沿邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Within the year he was transferred to overall frontier inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was made overall frontier inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時，金湯李欽、白豹神木馬兒、高羅跛臧三族尤悍難制，振募降羌，啖以利，令相攻，破十餘堡。

translations.literal: At the time the three tribes of Jintang Li Qin, Baibao Shenmu Ma'er, and Gaoluo Bozang were especially fierce and hard to control; Zhen recruited surrendered Qiang, fed them with profit, and had them attack one another, breaking more than ten forts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jintang Li Qin, Baibao Shenmu Ma'er, and Gaoluo Bozang tribes were especially fierce and hard to control. Zhen recruited surrendered Qiang, tempted them with rewards, and set them against one another, destroying more than ten forts.

sentences.zh: 欽等詣振自歸。

translations.literal: Qin and the others came to Zhen and submitted of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and the others came to Zhen and surrendered voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 振為置酒，先釂，取細仗，圍財數分，植百步外共射。

translations.literal: Zhen set out wine for them, drank first, took slender weapons, piled wealth in several portions, set them a hundred paces away, and they shot together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen set out wine for them and drank first. He took slender weapons, piled up several heaps of valuables a hundred paces away, and they shot at them together.

sentences.zh: 欽等百發不中，振十矢皆貫，欽等皆驚，誓不復敢犯。

translations.literal: Qin and the others shot a hundred times without hitting; Zhen's ten arrows all pierced through; Qin and the others were all astonished and swore never again to dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and his men shot a hundred times without hitting once, while Zhen's ten arrows all pierced clean through. They were astonished and swore never to offend again.

sentences.zh: 明年，涇原屬羌胡薩逋歌等叛，鈐轄王懷信以兵數千屬振遊奕，屢捷。

translations.literal: The next year the subordinate Qiang Hu Sabuge and others of Jingyuan rebelled; military commissioner Wang Huaixin assigned several thousand troops to Zhen for roaming patrol, and he repeatedly prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Jingyuan Qiang chieftain Hu Sabuge and others rebelled. Military commissioner Wang Huaixin assigned several thousand troops to Zhen for roaming patrol, and he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 從數十騎詣懷信，遇賊十倍，射殪數十，餘悉退散。

translations.literal: With several tens of horsemen he went to Huaixin; he met bandits ten times his number, shot and killed several tens, and the rest all withdrew and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: With only a few dozen horsemen he went to join Huaixin and met an enemy force ten times his size. He shot down dozens of them and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 數月，賊數萬圍平遠砦，都監趙士龍戰沒。

translations.literal: Several months later bandits numbering tens of thousands besieged Pingyuan Stockade; overall supervisor Zhao Shilong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later tens of thousands of bandits besieged Pingyuan Stockade, and overall supervisor Zhao Shilong was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 振出別道，力戰抵砦，奪取水泉，率敢死士破圍，賊走，追斬數千級，徙涇原都鹽，歷知順安、保安、廣信軍、霸州，改京東都大提舉捉賊。

translations.literal: Zhen went out by a separate route, fought fiercely to reach the stockade, seized the water spring, led dare-to-die troops to break the encirclement; the bandits fled; he pursued and beheaded several thousand; was transferred to overall salt commissioner of Jingyuan; successively governed Shun'an, Bao'an, Guangxin Army, and Bazhou; was changed to overall commissioner for apprehending bandits in eastern capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen took a separate route, fought his way to the stockade, seized its water supply, and led dare-to-die troops to break the siege. The enemy fled and he pursued them, taking several thousand heads. He was made overall salt commissioner of Jingyuan, served in turn as prefect of Shun'an, Bao'an, Guangxin Army, and Bazhou, and was appointed overall commissioner for apprehending bandits in the eastern capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，知環州，累遷象州防禦使。

translations.literal: The next year he governed Huanzhou; through successive promotions he became defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed to govern Huanzhou and rose through successive promotions to defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊將反，為金銀冠珮隱飾甲騎遺屬羌，振潛以金帛誘取之，以破其勢，得冠珮銀鞍三千、甲騎數百。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao was about to rebel, he sent gold and silver crowns and pendants concealing armored horsemen as gifts to subordinate Qiang; Zhen secretly used gold and silks to lure and take them, thereby breaking their momentum; he obtained three thousand crown pendants and silver saddles and several hundred armored horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao was preparing to rebel, he sent gold and silver crowns and pendants concealing armored horsemen as gifts to subordinate Qiang tribes. Zhen secretly used gold and silks to lure them away, breaking Yuanhao's buildup of strength. He obtained three thousand crowns, pendants, and silver saddles along with several hundred armored horsemen.

sentences.zh: 告鄰部俾以環為法，不聽，於是東茭、金明、萬劉諸族勝兵數萬，悉為賊所有。

translations.literal: He informed neighboring departments to take Huan as their model; they did not listen; thereby the Dongjiao, Jinming, Wanliu, and other tribes' crack troops numbering tens of thousands all fell into the bandits' possession.
translations.idiomatic: He urged neighboring prefectures to follow Huan's example, but they would not listen. Thereupon the crack troops of the Dongjiao, Jinming, Wanliu, and other tribes, numbering tens of thousands, all fell into the enemy's hands.

sentences.zh: 及劉平等皆敗，唯環慶無患。

translations.literal: When Liu Ping and others were all defeated, only Huan and Qing were without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ping and the others were defeated, only Huan and Qing remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 自本路馬步軍副總管擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、鄜延路副都總管、知延州，代范雍。

translations.literal: From vice overall commander of cavalry and infantry on this route he was promoted to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, vice overall commander of Fuyan route, and prefect of Yanzhou, replacing Fan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from vice overall commander of cavalry and infantry on his circuit to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, vice overall commander of the Fuyan circuit, and prefect of Yanzhou, replacing Fan Yong.

sentences.zh: 尋改捧日、天武四廂。

translations.literal: Shortly he was changed to the four wings of the Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to command of the four wings of the Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial guards.

sentences.zh: 振謂將吏曰：「今賊以我夷傷，必乘勝以進，勢宜固守。

translations.literal: Zhen said to the generals and officials: "Now the bandits, because we have suffered tribal wounds, will surely press the victory and advance; the situation calls for firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told his officers, "The enemy will take advantage of our tribal losses and press their victory. The situation calls for holding firm.

sentences.zh: 尚慮諸城不能皆如吾謀，苟延州弗支，則陝西未可測，此天下安危之機也。」

translations.literal: I still fear the various cities cannot all follow our plan; if Yanzhou cannot hold, then Shaanxi cannot be foreseen—this is the pivot of the empire's safety and peril."
translations.idiomatic: I still fear not every city can follow our plan. If Yanzhou cannot hold, Shaanxi's fate will be impossible to predict. This is the hinge on which the empire's safety turns."

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊寇塞門砦。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits raided Saimen Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy raided Saimen Stockade.

sentences.zh: 振有兵幾八千，按甲不動。

translations.literal: Zhen had troops of nearly eight thousand and kept his armor still without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had nearly eight thousand troops but held them motionless.

sentences.zh: 砦中兵才千人，屢告急，被圍五月，才遣百餘人赴之，砦遂陷。

translations.literal: The stockade had only a thousand troops; they repeatedly reported urgency; besieged for five months, he only then sent a little more than a hundred men to go to their aid; the stockade thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade had only a thousand men and sent repeated urgent appeals. After five months under siege, Zhen sent only a little over a hundred men to their aid, and the stockade fell.

sentences.zh: 砦主高延德、鹽押王繼元皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: Stockade commander Gao Yande and salt transport officer Wang Jiyuan both perished at the hands of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Stockade commander Gao Yande and salt transport officer Wang Jiyuan both perished at the enemy's hands.

sentences.zh: 振坐擁兵不救，為都轉運使龐籍所奏，貶白州團練使、知絳州。

translations.literal: Zhen was punished for holding troops and not rescuing; he was memorialized by overall transport commissioner Pang Ji and demoted to regimental commissioner of Baizhou and prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was punished for holding his troops back and not rescuing the stockade. Overall transport commissioner Pang Ji memorialized against him, and he was demoted to regimental commissioner of Baizhou and prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，會延德、繼元家復訴於朝，敕御史方偕就劾振。

translations.literal: He had not yet departed when Yande's and Jiyuan's families again appealed at court; an edict ordered censor Fang Xie to go and impeach Zhen on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, the families of Yande and Jiyuan appealed again at court. An edict ordered censor Fang Xie to go and investigate Zhen on the spot.

sentences.zh: 法當斬，再貶太子左清道率府率、潭州安置。

translations.literal: By law he should be beheaded; he was demoted again to colonel of the Left Pure Way of the Heir Apparent's Guard and assigned to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By law he deserved execution. He was demoted again to colonel of the Left Pure Way of the Heir Apparent's Guard and exiled to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復右武衛將軍、惠州團練使、幷代路兵馬鈐轄，就遷副總管、祁州團練使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was restored to general of the Right Martial Guard, regimental commissioner of Huizhou, and military commissioner of cavalry and horses on the Bing-Dai route; he was then promoted to vice overall commander and regimental commissioner of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was restored to general of the Right Martial Guard, made regimental commissioner of Huizhou and military commissioner of the Bing-Dai circuit, and then promoted to vice overall commander and regimental commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊既破豐州，將襲近砦，振率鈐轄張亢、麥允言出麟州深柏堰，擊破之。

translations.literal: After Yuanhao had broken Fengzhou and was about to raid nearby stockades, Zhen led military commissioners Zhang Kang and Mai Yunyan out from Shenbai Weir of Linzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanhao captured Fengzhou and was about to raid nearby stockades, Zhen led military commissioners Zhang Kang and Mai Yunyan out from Shenbai Weir near Linzhou and defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 兼領嵐、憲六州軍事。

translations.literal: He concurrently held military affairs of the six prefectures Lan and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He was also put in charge of military affairs in the six prefectures of Lan and Xian.

sentences.zh: 河外饑，振設法通砦外商，得米數十萬斛，軍民以濟。

translations.literal: When the region beyond the Yellow River suffered famine, Zhen devised methods to open trade with merchants outside the stockades, obtained several hundred thousand hu of rice, and army and people were thereby sustained.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the region beyond the Yellow River, Zhen devised a way to open trade with merchants outside the stockades and obtained several hundred thousand hu of grain, sustaining both army and people.

sentences.zh: 進博州防禦使，改解州致仕。

translations.literal: He advanced to defense commissioner of Bozhou and changed to retirement at Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defense commissioner of Bozhou and then retired at Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 復起為左神武軍大將軍，卒。

translations.literal: He was again raised as great general of the Left Divine Martial Army and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as great general of the Left Divine Martial Army and died in office.

sentences.zh: 振剛強自負，有武力，便弓馬，喜謀畫，輕財尚氣，眾樂為用。

translations.literal: Zhen was firm and strong, self-confident, possessed martial force, skilled with bow and horse, fond of planning, light with wealth and valuing spirit; the masses gladly served under him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was tough and self-confident, physically powerful, skilled with bow and horse, fond of strategy, generous with money and valuing honor. Men gladly followed him.

sentences.zh: 子珣、瑜，皆工騎射。

translations.literal: His sons Xun and Yu were both skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xun and Yu were both expert horsemen and archers.

sentences.zh: 珣年十六，仁宗召試便殿，授三班借職。

translations.literal: At age sixteen Xun was summoned by Emperor Renzong to be tested in the side hall and was given a borrowed post in the Third Class.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Xun was summoned by Emperor Renzong for testing in the side hall and granted a borrowed post in the Third Class.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，有言珣藝益進，且習書史。

translations.literal: During Jingyou it was said Xun's arts had further advanced and that he was also studying books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou era it was reported that Xun's martial skills had advanced further and that he was also studying history and the classics.

sentences.zh: 復召見閱武伎，又試策略於中書，條對數千言。

translations.literal: He was again summoned for audience to review martial arts; he was also tested in strategy at the Secretariat, and answered item by item in several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again to demonstrate his martial skills and tested in strategy at the Secretariat, where he submitted answers running to several thousand words.

sentences.zh: 自殿直進閤門祗候，未幾，除濠州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: From palace attendant direct he advanced to gatekeeper attendant; before long he was appointed overall military supervisor of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced from palace attendant direct to gatekeeper attendant and soon afterward was appointed overall military supervisor of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，珣隨父在西邊，訪得五路徼外形勝利害，作《聚米圖經》五卷。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xun followed his father on the western frontier, he investigated the terrain advantages and disadvantages along the five routes' borderlands and composed five scrolls of the Piled-Millet Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while following his father on the western frontier, Xun surveyed the strategic terrain along the five frontier routes and wrote the five-scroll Piled-Millet Gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 詔取其書，並召珣至，又上《五陣圖》、《兵事》十餘篇。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his book taken; Xun was also summoned to court and further presented more than ten chapters on the Five Formations Diagram and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his book brought to court and summoned Xun as well. He also presented more than ten chapters on the Five Formations Diagram and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝給步騎使按陣，既成，臨觀之。

translations.literal: The Emperor provided infantry and cavalry to arrange formations according to his diagrams; when it was done, he viewed it in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor provided infantry and cavalry to drill formations according to his diagrams, and when the drill was complete he watched it in person.

sentences.zh: 陳執中招討陝西，薦為緣邊巡檢使。

translations.literal: Chen Zhizhong was appointed to campaign against Shaanxi and recommended him as frontier patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zhizhong was appointed to campaign in Shaanxi, he recommended Xun as frontier patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 呂夷簡、宋庠為奏曰：「用兵以來，策士之言以萬計，無如珣者。

translations.literal: Lü Yijian and Song Xiu memorialized saying: "Since troops have been used, strategists' words number in the tens of thousands—none equal Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yijian and Song Xiu memorialized, "Since the war began, strategists have submitted tens of thousands of proposals, but none equal Xun's."

sentences.zh: 」即擢通事舍人、招討都監。

translations.literal: " He was immediately promoted to Communications Envoy and overall campaign supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately promoted to Communications Envoy and overall campaign supervisor.

sentences.zh: 珣自以年少新進，辭都監。

translations.literal: Xun considered himself young and newly advanced and declined the post of overall supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, considering himself young and newly advanced, declined the post of overall supervisor.

sentences.zh: 授兵萬人，御賜鎧仗，令自擇偏裨、參佐，居涇原，兼治籠竿城。

translations.literal: He was given ten thousand troops, imperially bestowed armor and weapons, ordered to choose his own lieutenants and staff, stationed at Jingyuan, and concurrently governed Longgan city.
translations.idiomatic: He was given ten thousand troops and imperially bestowed armor and weapons, allowed to choose his own lieutenants and staff, stationed at Jingyuan, and put in charge of Longgan city as well.

sentences.zh: 麻氈、黨留百餘帳處近塞為暴，珣白府，引兵二萬，自靜邊歷揆吳抵木寧襲賊，俘獲數千計。

translations.literal: More than a hundred tents of Mazhan and Dangliu near the border committed violence; Xun reported to the prefecture, led twenty thousand troops from Jingbian through Kuiwu to Muning to strike the bandits, and captured several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred tents of the Mazhan and Dangliu tribes near the border were raiding. Xun reported to headquarters, led twenty thousand troops from Jingbian through Kuiwu to Muning to strike the enemy, and captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 靜邊將劉滬殿後，為賊所掩。

translations.literal: Jingbian commander Liu Hu brought up the rear and was ambushed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbian commander Liu Hu brought up the rear and was ambushed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 珣登阪望見，從騎數百復入，拔滬之眾以出，士皆歎服。

translations.literal: Xun climbed a slope and saw it; with several hundred followers he entered again, extricated Hu's force, and the soldiers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Xun climbed a slope and saw what had happened. With a few hundred horsemen he charged back in, rescued Liu Hu's force, and all the soldiers marveled at his daring.

sentences.zh: 瞎氈居龕穀無所屬，珣與書招之，遺以綈綿，瞎氈聽命。

translations.literal: Xiazhan dwelt in Kan Valley without allegiance; Xun wrote to summon him, sent silk and cotton as gifts, and Xiazhan obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazhan lived in Kan Valley without allegiance to either side. Xun wrote to win him over, sent him silks and cotton, and Xiazhan submitted.

sentences.zh: 改本路都監，詔追入朝。

translations.literal: He was changed to overall supervisor of this route; an edict recalled him to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made overall supervisor of his circuit and recalled to court by edict.

sentences.zh: 將行，適元昊大入，府檄留珣，會葛懷敏於瓦亭。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, it happened that Yuanhao made a major invasion; the prefecture's dispatch ordered Xun retained; he joined Ge Huaimin at Wating.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to leave, Yuanhao launched a major invasion. Headquarters ordered Xun to remain and join Ge Huaimin at Wating.

sentences.zh: 懷敏已屯五谷口西至馬欄城，聞夏人徙軍新壕外，議欲質明掩襲。

translations.literal: Huaimin had already encamped from Wugu Pass west to Malan city; hearing the Xia had moved their army outside the new moat, they discussed making a dawn raid by appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin had already encamped from Wugu Pass west to Malan city. Hearing that the Xia had moved their army outside the new moat, his officers discussed a surprise attack at dawn.

sentences.zh: 珣謂懷敏曰：「敵遠來，眾倍鋒銳，莫若依馬欄城布柵以扼其路，守鎮戎城以便餉道，俟其衰擊之，此必勝之道也。

translations.literal: Xun said to Huaimin: "The enemy has come from afar; their numbers double ours and their edge is sharp—better to rely on Malan city, set palisades to choke their route, hold Zhenrong city to ease the supply road, wait until they weaken and then strike—this is the way certain to win.
translations.idiomatic: Xun told Huaimin, "The enemy has come from far away with numbers twice ours and their morale at its peak. Better to fortify Malan city with palisades to block their advance, hold Zhenrong city to secure our supply line, and strike when they weaken. That is the sure way to victory.

sentences.zh: 不然，必為賊所屠。

translations.literal: Otherwise you will surely be slaughtered by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we shall be slaughtered by the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」懷敏不聽，兵遂逼鎮戎城，越界壕，抵定川。

translations.literal: " Huaimin did not listen; the army then pressed Zhenrong city, crossed the border moat, and reached Dingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin would not listen. The army pressed on to Zhenrong city, crossed the border moat, and reached Dingchuan.

sentences.zh: 未及陣，夏人引鐵騎來犯，珣居陣西北，瑜亦在軍中，戰甚力。

translations.literal: Before they could form battle lines, the Xia led iron cavalry to attack; Xun held the northwest of the formation; Yu was also in the army and fought very fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could form battle lines, Xia iron cavalry attacked. Xun held the northwest wing and Yu was also in the army, fighting fiercely.

sentences.zh: 東壁兵輒潰，中軍大擾，珣擁刀斧手前鬥，夏眾稍卻，我軍復陣。

translations.literal: The eastern wing troops immediately collapsed; the central army was greatly disturbed; Xun led sword and axe men forward to fight; the Xia force slightly withdrew; our army re-formed.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern wing collapsed at once and the center fell into chaos. Xun led his sword-and-axe men forward and the Xia force gave ground slightly, allowing our army to re-form.

sentences.zh: 懷敏詰朝退走，就食鎮戎。

translations.literal: Huaimin at dawn the next day retreated and went to take food at Zhenrong.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day Huaimin retreated to Zhenrong to obtain provisions.

sentences.zh: 俄夏騎四合，珣被擒，瑜以身免。

translations.literal: Shortly Xia horsemen closed in on all four sides; Xun was captured; Yu escaped by his own body.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xia horsemen closed in from all sides. Xun was captured and Yu escaped by his own efforts.

sentences.zh: 珣美風儀，性勁特好學，恂恂類儒者。

translations.literal: Xun had fine bearing; by nature he was firm and special, fond of learning, respectful and mild like a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had a fine bearing. By nature he was resolute, loved learning, and in manner was as courteous as a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 既沒，人多惜之。

translations.literal: After he perished, many people regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death many mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 贈莫州刺史，後卒賊中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given prefect of Mozhou; later he died among the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Mozhou and later died in enemy hands.

sentences.zh: 瑜弟璞，亦知名。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Pu was also well known.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Pu was also well known.

sentences.zh: 范恪，字許國，開封人。

translations.literal: Fan Ke, style name Xuguo, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ke, whose style name was Xuguo, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初名全，少隸軍籍於許州，選入捧日軍，又選為殿前指揮使，歷行門、龍旗直、散員押班。

translations.literal: His original name was Quan; in youth he entered army rolls at Xuzhou; was selected into the Sun-Bearer Army; again selected as palace-front commander; successively served in the Gate Squad, Dragon Banner Direct, and Scattered Member Escort Leader.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Quan. In his youth he entered army rolls at Xuzhou, was selected into the Sun-Bearer Army, and then chosen as palace-front commander, serving in turn in the Gate Squad, Dragon Banner Direct, and Scattered Member Escort Leader posts.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，元昊數寇邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding Yuanhao repeatedly raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Kangding era Yuanhao raided the frontier repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 試武伎，擢內殿崇班、慶州北路都巡檢使，與攻白豹城，破之。

translations.literal: He was tested in martial arts, promoted to Inner Hall Honored Company, overall northern-route inspector of Qingzhou, joined in attacking Baibao city, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Tested in martial arts, he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Company and made overall inspector of the northern route of Qingzhou. He joined the attack on Baibao city and captured it.

sentences.zh: 既還，夏人遣騎襲其後。

translations.literal: After they returned, the Xia sent horsemen to strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, Xia horsemen attacked from the rear.

sentences.zh: 恪設伏崖險，敵半度，邀擊之，斬首四百級，生獲七十餘人。

translations.literal: Ke set an ambush on a precipitous cliff; when the enemy were half across, he intercepted and struck them, beheading four hundred and capturing more than seventy alive.
translations.idiomatic: Ke laid an ambush on a steep cliff. When the enemy were half across, he attacked, taking four hundred heads and more than seventy prisoners.

sentences.zh: 以功遷內殿承制。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Inner Hall Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to Inner Hall Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘗會諸道兵攻十二盤暨咄當、迷子砦，中流矢，督戰愈力。

translations.literal: He once joined troops from all routes to attack Shierpan and the Zhuodang and Mizi stockades; he was struck by a stray arrow and directed battle all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: He once joined forces from several circuits to attack Shierpan and the Zhuodang and Mizi stockades. Struck by a stray arrow, he pressed the attack all the harder.

sentences.zh: 視炮石中有火爨者，恪取號於眾曰：「賊矢石盡，用灶下甓矣。

translations.literal: Seeing among the catapult stones some with cooking fires, Ke took up a shout to the masses saying: "The bandits' arrows and stones are exhausted—they are using bricks from beneath the stove.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing among the catapult stones some still warm from cooking fires, Ke shouted to his men, "The enemy have run out of missiles—they are hurling bricks from their camp stoves!

sentences.zh: 」於是士卒爭奮，果先得城。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the soldiers vied in ardor and indeed took the city first.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers fought all the harder and were first to take the city.

sentences.zh: 遷供備庫副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the supply depot.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the supply depot.

sentences.zh: 恪有弓勝一石七斗，其箭鏃如鏵，名曰鏵弓。

translations.literal: Ke had a bow exceeding one stone and seven dou in draw; its arrowheads were like plowshares, and it was called the Plowshare Bow.
translations.idiomatic: Ke wielded a bow with a draw weight of more than one stone and seven dou. Its arrowheads were shaped like plowshares, and the weapon was called the Plowshare Bow.

sentences.zh: 又於羽間識其官稱、姓氏，凡所發必中，至一箭貫二人。

translations.literal: He also marked his office title and surname between the feathers; every shot he loosed invariably hit, even to one arrow piercing two men.
translations.idiomatic: He also marked his rank and name on the fletching. Every shot hit its mark, and on one occasion a single arrow pierced two men.

sentences.zh: 他日，取蕉蒿砦歸，恪獨殿後，為數千騎所襲。

translations.literal: Another day, returning from taking Jiaogao Stockade, Ke alone brought up the rear and was attacked by several thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, returning from the capture of Jiaogao Stockade, Ke alone brought up the rear and was attacked by several thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 屬視矢箙止有二鏵，即為引滿之勢，賊遽卻。

translations.literal: It happened that looking in his arrow quiver he had only two plowshare arrows left; he at once made the motion of drawing to the full, and the bandits immediately withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Glancing at his quiver, he found only two Plowshare arrows left. He drew his bow to the full as if to shoot, and the enemy withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 嘗與總管杜惟序、鈐轄高繼隆將兵分討漢乞、薛馬、都嵬等三砦，恪先破都嵬，而繼隆圍薛馬不能下，恪馳往取之，既又援惟序下漢乞砦。

translations.literal: He once with overall commander Du Weixu and military commissioner Gao Jilong led troops in separate campaigns against the three stockades Hanqi, Xuema, and Duwei; Ke first broke Duwei, while Jilong besieged Xuema and could not take it—Ke galloped to seize it, then again aided Weixu in taking Hanqi Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He once campaigned with overall commander Du Weixu and military commissioner Gao Jilong against the three stockades of Hanqi, Xuema, and Duwei. Ke first captured Duwei. When Jilong besieged Xuema without success, Ke galloped to take it, then went to aid Weixu in capturing Hanqi Stockade.

sentences.zh: 改左騏驥副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Qiji Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Qiji Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 虜犯大順城，諸將皆閉城自守。

translations.literal: When the barbarians attacked Dashun city, all the generals closed the city and held themselves in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy attacked Dashun city, the other generals shut themselves inside and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 恪率兵二千餘，戰克之。

translations.literal: Ke led a little more than two thousand troops and defeated them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ke led a little over two thousand men into battle and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 改宮苑副使、環慶路兵馬都監，因特召見。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice commissioner of the palace park and overall military supervisor of the Huanqing route, and was specially summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of the palace park and overall military supervisor of the Huanqing circuit and was specially summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗謂曰：「適有邊奏，賊犯高平軍劉璠堡，可乘驛亟往。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said to him: "There has just been a frontier report that bandits have attacked Liu Fan's fort at Gaoping Army—you may take the post relay and go quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong told him, "A frontier report has just arrived: the enemy have attacked Liu Fan's fort at Gaoping Army. Take the post roads and go at once.

sentences.zh: 」遂遷禮賓使、榮州刺史、環慶路鈐轄，手詔令趣范仲淹麾下起兵赴援。

translations.literal: " He was then transferred to Communications Envoy, prefect of Rongzhou, and military commissioner of Huanqing route; an imperial autograph edict ordered him to hurry to Fan Zhongyan's command to raise troops and go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Communications Envoy, prefect of Rongzhou, and military commissioner of the Huanqing circuit. An imperial autograph edict ordered him to join Fan Zhongyan's command, raise troops, and hurry to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 恪晝夜兼行，比至平涼，賊已解。

translations.literal: Ke traveled day and night without pause; by the time he reached Pingliang, the bandits had already dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Ke traveled day and night without rest, but by the time he reached Pingliang the enemy had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷洛苑使，權秦鳳路兵馬總管。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Luoyuan Commissioner and acting overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Qinfeng route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Luoyuan Commissioner and acting overall commander of the Qinfeng circuit.

sentences.zh: 恪驍勇善射，臨難敢前，故數有戰功，自龍、神衛四廂都指揮使累遷至侍衛親軍馬步軍副都指揮使，曆坊州刺史、解州防禦、宣州觀察使、保信軍節度觀察留後，以疾出為永興軍路副都總管，數月卒，贈昭化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Ke was fierce and brave, skilled at archery, daring to advance in peril; therefore he repeatedly won battle merit. From overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Spirit guards he was promoted through successive steps to vice overall commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry and infantry; he successively served as prefect of Fangzhou, defense commissioner of Jiezhou, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou, and regent military governor and observer of Baoxin Army; because of illness he went out as vice overall commander of Yongxing Army route; several months later he died and was posthumously given military governor of Zhaohua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was fierce, brave, and an expert archer who always pressed forward in danger, and he won repeated victories. He rose from overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon and Spirit guards to vice overall commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry and infantry, served in turn as prefect of Fangzhou, defense commissioner of Jiezhou, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou, and regent military governor of the Baoxin army, then left office because of illness to serve as vice overall commander of the Yongxing Army circuit. He died several months later and was posthumously enfeoffed as military governor of the Zhaohua army.

sentences.zh: 馬懷德

translations.literal: Ma Huaide
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huaide

sentences.zh: 馬懷德，字得之，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Ma Huaide, style name Dezhi, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huaide, whose style name was Dezhi, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
